macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. tech stocks suffer sharp selloff as oil rises
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.6% as investors reduced exposure to technology stocks and moved into Treasurys, pushing yields sharply lower. Brent crude rose above $111 a barrel amid attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and concerns about potential U.S.-Iran tensions disrupting supplies.

items.title: U.S. stocks open mixed ahead of Federal Reserve decision
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.30% and the S&P 500 gained 0.12%, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.14%. Markets priced in an 89.6% probability of a 25-basis-point Fed rate cut, with the central bank’s policy meeting beginning Tuesday and concluding Wednesday.

items.title: U.S. weekly jobless claims decline
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims fell to 194,000 for the week ended October 17, down from a revised 200,000 the previous week, indicating continued resilience in the labor market.

items.title: South Korea central bank pauses tightening cycle
items.summary: The Bank of Korea held its policy rate unchanged after two consecutive increases, as inflation eased but remained above the central bank’s target.

items.title: Japan inflation strengthens expectations for December rate hike
items.summary: Japan’s consumer prices excluding fresh food rose 2.1% year over year in September, reinforcing market expectations that the Bank of Japan could tighten policy in December.

items.title: Meta’s AI spending plans unsettle investors
items.summary: Meta’s efforts to secure funding for large-scale artificial-intelligence investment contributed to concerns about the cost and sustainability of the sector’s capital spending, adding to the broader technology selloff.

items.title: European consumer confidence deteriorates
items.summary: The European Commission’s flash consumer-confidence indicator for the euro area fell 1.1 points to minus 17.9 in October, below economists’ expectation of minus 17.0.

items.title: Home Depot outlook pressures shares
items.summary: Home Depot shares fell 2.5% after the home-improvement retailer forecast fiscal 2026 comparable-sales growth and profit below analyst expectations.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin drops below $80,000 amid broad crypto sell-off
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $80,000, down about 3.4% over 24 hours, while more than $91 million in crypto positions were liquidated in one hour. Ether liquidations totaled roughly $13.4 million.[1]

items.title: Bitcoin spot ETFs record $635 million net outflow
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw approximately $635.5 million in net outflows on Thursday as Bitcoin and other major tokens declined.[1]

items.title: Russia proposes regulated crypto access with investor limits
items.summary: Russia’s central bank proposed allowing Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on regulated exchanges, while limiting annual purchases by non-qualified investors to 300,000 rubles per intermediary.[1]

items.title: Russia plans restrictions on direct crypto peer-to-peer transfers
items.summary: Updated Bank of Russia guidance says direct individual-to-individual crypto transactions will be phased out by July 2027, with transactions required to use authorized intermediaries. Transfers to self-custodial wallets are also prohibited under the guidance.[1]

items.title: Polygon releases security update for Bor
items.summary: Polygon Labs released Bor v2.10.3 to address two medium-severity denial-of-service vulnerabilities affecting parallel block execution. The flaws were disclosed through Immunefi’s bug bounty program.[1]

items.title: Coinbase Ireland fined €3.25 million by central bank
items.summary: Ireland’s central bank fined Coinbase Ireland €3.25 million for failures involving customer-fund safeguards and oversight of outsourced operations.[1]

items.title: Chainlink partners with LG CNS on Korean digital-asset infrastructure
items.summary: Chainlink is partnering with LG Group technology affiliate LG CNS to develop compliant digital-asset infrastructure for South Korea’s market.[1]

items.title: Mesh and Visa expand crypto payment functionality
items.summary: Crypto payments firm Mesh partnered with Visa to allow participating wallet applications to make in-store and online payments from users’ crypto, stablecoin or fiat balances.[1]

items.title: JPMorgan commits $100 million to Solana real-world assets
items.summary: JPMorgan reportedly committed $100 million to real-world assets on Solana, expanding its blockchain activity beyond its existing Ethereum-based dollar-deposit token.[1]

items.title: Visa acquisition report disputed by Fireblocks
items.summary: Fireblocks denied reports that Visa was negotiating a $2.5 billion acquisition of the digital-asset infrastructure company.[1]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft AI diagnostic system reportedly outperforms doctors on complex cases
items.summary: Microsoft researchers developed a diagnostic orchestrator that coordinates AI agents to reason through difficult medical cases. Reports say it achieved substantially higher accuracy than general physicians, though clinical evaluation with hospitals and patients is still planned.

items.title: Canva launches its first image-generation model
items.summary: Canva released Canva Craft, an image-generation model trained around human-designed templates and intended to compete with leading image tools from major AI companies.

items.title: Uber expands OpenAI enterprise AI access to global workforce
items.summary: Uber rolled out ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees after a pilot involving 1,000 workers. Employees can use it for research, meeting preparation, presentations, data analysis and workflow automation.

items.title: ASI raises $325 million at $3 billion valuation
items.summary: Artificial intelligence startup ASI raised $325 million as investors continued to back AI software aimed at practical, real-world applications.

items.title: Hugging Face releases open-weight Carbon-X model for DNA analysis
items.summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, a 14-billion-parameter decoder-only model trained on 300 billion tokens that allows users to query DNA sequences using natural language.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly nears a new financing round
items.summary: Market reports indicate that OpenAI is close to completing another fundraising round, amid continued investor demand for frontier AI companies.

items.title: Chinese AI labs expand self-hosted and overseas model availability
items.summary: Reports say DeepSeek and MiniMax completed open-source and overseas licensing efforts, while a large Chinese mixture-of-experts model became available for self-hosting by developers.

items.title: AI reshapes entry-level technology hiring
items.summary: AI adoption is increasing pressure on entry-level technology jobs, particularly in India, as employers adjust hiring needs and automate or augment traditional junior roles.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA cuts 400 jobs and closes BioWare
items.summary: Electronic Arts is cutting about 400 positions, closing BioWare, and restructuring several projects. The changes reportedly include pausing The Sims Project Lotus, canceling a new Mass Effect project, and ending a joint Respawn-DICE project.

items.title: EA pauses second Sims project amid restructuring
items.summary: EA has reportedly paused development of Project Lotus, a second Sims title, while prioritizing Project Evergreen. The restructuring also affects BioWare, a smaller skate. team, and other unannounced projects.

items.title: Half-Life 3 speculation intensifies after Valve developer mentions HLX
items.summary: A Valve developer reportedly referenced “HLX” during a convention panel, renewing speculation that it is the codename for the next Half-Life game. The report says alleged insiders claim the title is far enough along for full-game testing.

items.title: Activision studio Elsewhere begins hiring for open-world game
items.summary: Activision-owned studio Elsewhere has posted recruitment listings for an unannounced open-world project focused on systemic gameplay and dynamic environmental interactions. The project would expand Activision’s portfolio beyond its traditionally linear shooter franchises.

items.title: Marvel’s Wolverine leads projected US September sales chart
items.summary: Marvel’s Wolverine reportedly topped projected US game sales for September 2026, ahead of NBA 2K27 and EA Sports FC 27. PlayStation 5 also led monthly US hardware sales, with consumer spending reported up year over year.

items.title: EA announces return of Fight Night
items.summary: EA has announced that a new Fight Night boxing game is in pre-production, using the company’s simulation fighting team. The announcement comes alongside a broader restructuring of EA’s development projects.

items.title: Indonesia gaming industry projected to add $3.3 billion by 2030
items.summary: A Tencent and Access Partnership report projects that Indonesia’s gaming industry could contribute up to $3.3 billion in economic value and support about 476,600 jobs by 2030 under an accelerated-growth scenario.
